correctness.rationale: The expected infected count equals the uniform-source sum of percolation connectivities; on a tree every open path has probability p^{distance}, so (n-1)R(v,p)=sum over ordered residual connected pairs p^{distance}. Directly inspected RESULT.md and verify.py; a fresh independent finite exhaustive checker regenerated unlabelled tree class counts 1,1,2,3,6,11 for orders 2..7, checked a fixed minimizer in every class using exact polynomial root/sign tests, and independently reconstructed the n=8 witness F_2=7+8p+6p^2+4p^3+2p^4 and F_1=7+10p+6p^2+2p^3. Their difference 2p(p^3+p^2-1) has a unique interior root; all other target polynomials are dominated by a candidate globally. Finite enumeration is exhaustive here because leaf deletion recovers every unlabelled tree and the exact sign algorithm covers the entire probability interval; it is not an extrapolation to larger trees.

value.rationale: Whether one fixed intervention target minimizes expected infection irrespective of transmissibility is a natural network intervention question. The theorem supplies the complete sharp order-through-seven boundary and a concrete eight-vertex algebraic transition, separating topology-only selection from probability-dependent selection. This is mathematically motivated finite classification, not a cosmetic isolated calculation.

final_claim: For homogeneous independent-bond transmission on a finite tree with one preemptively removed vertex and a uniformly sampled surviving source, every unlabelled tree on at most seven vertices has a single optimum for every p in (0,1). The displayed eight-vertex tree has a unique optimum switch from vertex 2 to vertex 1 at the root of p^3+p^2=1 in (3/4,4/5), and order eight is minimal.
